    4. Iterates N times to read lists of strings from input, splits each line into a list, removes the first element, and appends the rest to S.
    5. Initializes a 2D list dp with dimensions (N+1) x (len(T)+1), where each element is set to 0 for the first column and INF (10^18) for the rest.
    6. Iterates over each list of strings in S.
    7. Copies the previous dp state to the current state when no strings are added.
    8. For each string in the current list, iterates over possible lengths of the target string T.
    9. Calculates the new length post_len after adding the current string.
    10. If post_len exceeds the length of T, breaks out of the loop.
    11. Checks if the concatenation of the current prefix of T and the current string matches the prefix of T up to post_len.
    12. If j is 0, sets dp[i][post_len] to 1.
    13. Otherwise, updates dp[i][post_len] to the minimum of its current value and dp[i-1][j] + 1.
    14. After processing all lists, checks if dp[N][len(T)] is greater than N.
    15. If it is, prints -1.
    16. Otherwise, prints dp[N][len(T)].
